analysis.title: Global Markets Daily: AI and The Dollar: Making It or Breaking It
key_insights: GS G10 FX strategy argues the Dollar is linked to AI-related equity performance. An AI selloff with rest-of-world outperformance was expected to be a catalyst for Dollar depreciation.
Recent price action shows the balance is fine. The AI correction took US relative equity performance off the highs, but DXY reached new highs.
Recent DXY moves are well explained by US 2-year yields, risk sentiment, and relative equity returns (Exhibit 1). Safe-haven characteristics have been clearly on display in recent weeks.

AI selloffs are most clearly USD negative when the broader risk backdrop stays supported, as on November 5 after the US midterm elections, which GS equity strategists called a rotation within equities.

When an AI selloff spills into broader risk sentiment, the Dollar tends to appreciate even with relative US equity underperformance. Some October days were exceptions, reflecting rate relief in European assets.
The share of days when the S&P 500 also falls during an AI selloff has risen, while the share when it rises has fallen. Cross-asset sentiment has become more sensitive to AI.

Policymakers are focused on the risk. Almost all FOMC minutes participants flagged AI investment disappointment under financial stability, and AI was the top concern in the Financial Stability Report survey.
Higher equity volatility makes the Dollar less sensitive to relative equity returns, so near-term Dollar weakness on AI selloffs is less likely.
Over the medium term a more negative AI view is still Dollar-negative. Weaker forward capex expectations and fading AI price pressures would erode support the Dollar had in 2026.

GS estimates AI contributed roughly one-third of cumulative DXY appreciation through October 2026, assuming AI drives most of the growth-expectations impulse and about half of the policy-rate impulse.

GS baseline is a gradual peaking of AI investment and less AI-led US equity outperformance, weighing on the Dollar over time. The key risk is a rapid reassessment that creates at least temporary Dollar demand.

The trade ideas list has 15 open positions across EM FX, rates, and equity pairs. Several are near targets or stops, such as long INR/IDR at 196 vs 200 target and long PHP 5Y bonds at 7.41% vs 7.00% target.

risk_factors: A rapid reassessment of AI, rather than the gradual one GS expects, could create at least temporary Dollar demand.
AI drawdowns may increasingly come with broader equity declines and higher equity volatility, so safe-haven flows dominate.
A reversal of AI impulses to US short-term rates and growth expectations could unwind the Dollar support they gave.
Policymakers' concern about AI investment disappointment is a financial stability risk.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 decomposes DXY into contributions implied by SPX, SPX/MSCI World ex US, and US 2Y yields vs actual DXY, with coefficients estimated on weekly changes 2010-2025.
Exhibit 9 shows cumulative AI contribution to DXY via 5y5y and 1y yields, with GS estimating roughly one-third of cumulative DXY appreciation through October 2026.
vol_and_positioning: As equity volatility rises, DXY beta to relative US vs ex-US equity returns falls, with the high-vol regime coefficient lower than the low-vol regime (Exhibit 7).
S&P 500 and GS AI basket 1-month rolling volatility rose in recent weeks (Exhibit 8).
The share of AI-selloff days with SPX also down, on a 3-month rolling window, has risen relative to the 2023-2025 average (Exhibit 5).
geopolitical: US midterm elections: the November 5 AI selloff after the vote was characterized by GS equity strategists as a rotation within equities.

tension_points.bull_case: Medium term, weaker AI capex expectations and fading AI price pressures erode Dollar support, so an AI selloff is Dollar-negative, especially when broader risk is supported.
tension_points.bear_case: Near term, AI selloffs increasingly spill into broader risk-off and higher equity volatility, so safe-haven demand lifts the Dollar, as DXY hitting new highs showed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rapid rather than gradual AI reassessment would produce at least temporary Dollar demand, undermining the gradual-peaking baseline.
